title: fix(pm): an authorised APPROVED review satisfies the queue guard on any commit (2026-09-04 ruling)
body:
Fixes #15187
Fixes #15209

⚠️ **This PR touches a governed surface, so it stays a DRAFT.** No seat flips it ready, enqueues it or arms auto-merge. It lands by the maintainer's own merge, or on one authorised approval — which, under the very predicate this PR carries, no longer expires when the branch moves.

## The ruling

Maintainer, 2026-09-04, live PM chat, verbatim and untranslated — said while a governed PR that an authorised approver had approved three times kept falling out of the merge queue:

> 你的门禁有问题，只需要有人工批准记录就行，不需要卡最新的提交。

It supersedes the sha-pin half of the 2026-08-27 predicate. The approver set of that ruling (「os-zhuang hotlong 批准算数」) stands unchanged.

## The predicate, before and after

`scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs`, the `merge_group` leg:

| | before (2026-08-27) | after (2026-09-04) |
|:---|:---|:---|
| authorised approval on the CURRENT head | passes | passes |
| authorised approval on an OLDER commit | **refuses** (stale) | **passes** |
| approval with no `commit_id` at all | refuses | passes |
| unauthorised account, APPROVED | refuses | refuses |
| DISMISSED, or superseded by the same reviewer's later CHANGES_REQUESTED | refuses | refuses |
| empty review list | refuses | refuses |
| review list unreadable | refuses, exit 4 | refuses, exit 4 |
| PR head unreadable | refuses, exit 4 | **printed as a missing reading; the reviews still judge** |

The accepted cost is stated out loud in the header rather than left to be discovered: a push after an approval is no longer re-reviewed by this gate. It is the same shape of cost the 2026-08-12 ruling on the retired per-PR gate accepted when it dropped the identity proxy (「不要指定具体的人」); the institutional-memory section of `scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs` carries that history.

The PR head is still read, so a cleared queue log can name the commit each approval was given on — that is where the accepted cost becomes visible at the moment it is paid. But it decides nothing, so its own read failure is no longer a refusal: a read that decides nothing may not block a landing. The review list, which IS the predicate's input, still refuses.

### Two renames, landed with their only importer

| before | after | why |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `pinnedApprovalVerdict` | `authorizedApprovalVerdict` | it no longer pins anything |
| `staleApprovers` | `approvalsOnEarlierCommits` | a bucket named for a refusal is one a later reader re-derives a refusal from — these approvals now COUNT and are in `approvers` as well |

`.claude/hooks/guard-governed-enqueue.sh` imports that function and reads that bucket, which is the "no second mechanism" design paying off: the seat-side hook's verdict flipped with this ruling for free, and it needed no predicate of its own. It is also why the renames could not land alone — the hook catches an import failure and **allows**, with one warning line on stderr, so every governed enqueue would have sailed through it silently.

## The hook self-test, measured in three states

`.claude/hooks/guard-governed-enqueue.selftest.sh` is discovered and run by `lint.yml` as the job **Claude hook guard self-tests**, and it pinned the sha pin.

| tree | result |
|:---|:---|
| pre-ruling guard (measured by ablation: the `origin/main` copy of the one file restored on disk, hash-confirmed, then restored from HEAD) | **49 passed, 0 failed** |
| guard changed, hook untouched | **47 passed, 2 failed** |
| this PR | **50 passed, 0 failed** |

The two cases were flipped, not deleted. The fixture `governed-stale` became `governed-approved-on-an-earlier-commit`, and the case that asserted it BLOCKS now asserts it ALLOWS — the hook holds no predicate of its own, so that direction arrives entirely through the imported function, and reverting the guard would turn this case red. The case that asserted the refusal says "STALE approval" is replaced by two: one asserting the refusal states the ruled predicate, and one asserting the retired sentence is **absent**, through a new `expect_lacks` helper. A retired rule leaves its sentence behind in the text a seat actually reads long after the predicate stopped enforcing it, and only an absence assertion catches that.

The hook's blocking message also changed:

```
- 2. Wait for the APPROVED review to land on THIS head sha ($head_sha).
-    A push after the approval unpins it — re-request, do not re-enqueue.
+ 2. Wait for the APPROVED review to land. It does NOT have to sit on the
+    current head ($head_sha), and a later push does not expire it — maintainer,
+    2026-09-04: 只需要有人工批准记录就行，不需要卡最新的提交。
```

The `approvalsOnEarlierCommits` line is dropped from the hook's rendered detail: since the ruling that bucket can only be non-empty when the verdict is `approved`, and the detail string is only ever printed on the blocking path, so a line for it would be dead code that reads like a live refusal reason.

## The two prose sites

**`AGENTS.md`**, the governed-landing paragraph:

```
- **Those four lift only for an authorized approval pinned to the current head** (2026-08-27; guard
- 2026-08-28): APPROVED, by an account in `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` (...), `commit_id` = that sha — then the
- queue lands it, re-validating as it merges, and any later push expires it. […] Unpinned, the
- maintainer's bypass direct merge (人工直合) is the only landing.
+ **Those four lift only for an authorized APPROVED review** — by an account in `GOVERNED_APPROVERS`
+ (...), on ANY commit; the queue then lands it. Approver set 2026-08-27; pin retired 2026-09-04:
+ 「只需要有人工批准记录就行，不需要卡最新的提交。」 A later push no longer expires it, and this gate
+ does not re-review it. […] Unapproved, the bypass direct merge (人工直合) is the only landing.
```

**`.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md`**, the ACCEPT-fork clause — this one matters twice over, because it is the text every later PM dispatch reads:

```
- 或**授权人工批准钉 head ⇒ 队列放行**（2026-08-27 裁定）(… APPROVED 且 `commit_id`
- = PR 当前 head 才算,批准后再推提交即过期转红)。未钉批准 ⛔ 不翻 ready、不入队、不挂 auto-merge
+ 或**授权人工批准 ⇒ 队列放行**（2026-09-04 裁定,逐字「只需要有人工批准记录就行，不需要卡最新的提交。」
+ ——取代 2026-08-27 的钉 head 半边,批准人集合不变)(… 授权账户 APPROVED 即算,⛔ 不卡 `commit_id`,
+ 批准后再推提交也不过期)。无批准 ⛔ 不翻 ready、不入队、不挂 auto-merge
```

Both rewrites are wrapped inside the 120-byte line budget, with the verbatim ruling kept whole on one line in each file — a soft line break inside 「」 renders as a space, and a quotation with a space in it is a quotation that was edited. The sentence in `AGENTS.md` that enumerates the governed surfaces is untouched, which `check:pm-governed-prose` asserts.

## Guard self-test

`node scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --self-test` — **133 cases pass**. The battery that pinned the sha pin is renamed and flipped; no battery was deleted, so `SELF_TEST_BATTERY_FLOOR` is untouched at 17. Cases now pinning the ruling in both directions:

- an authorised approval on an OLDER commit passes — asserted per account, iterating `GOVERNED_APPROVERS`
- an approval carrying no `commit_id` at all passes
- an unauthorised APPROVED refuses, and does not mask an authorised one on an older commit
- a DISMISSED authorised approval refuses; so does one superseded by the same reviewer's later CHANGES_REQUESTED
- an empty review list refuses; a COMMENTED review by an authorised account is not an approval
- an older commit is REPORTED in `approvalsOnEarlierCommits` and COUNTED in `approvers` at the same time
- an unreadable head reports no reading instead of failing closed
- end to end: an unreadable PR head no longer refuses, and the reviews are still read and still judge
- end to end: an authorised approval on an older commit clears the queue leg, and the log says it counted anyway
- the refusal text says an approval on an EARLIER commit would have counted, and never says STALE
- the `pull_request` early-warning leg stays byte-identical and head-read-free

## Untouched

The `pull_request` early-warning leg and its rendered output, the path test, the exit codes, the check-run name, `GOVERNED_APPROVERS`, the generated-surface register, and `.github/workflows/governed-surface-guard.yml`.

## Gates

Derived on the final tree with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --commands` (no paths) — 5 changed paths, 31 commands, no stale-tree warning. Every exit code captured before any pipe. Verification-run head sha: **`0a8763f6`**.

| gate | exit | verdict line |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `bash .claude/hooks/guard-governed-enqueue.selftest.sh` | 0 | `50 passed, 0 failed` |
| `node scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --self-test` | 0 | `✓ check-governed-queue-guard self-test: 133 cases pass` |
| `pnpm check:pm-skill-ratchet` | 0 | `AGENTS.md is 1161 lines (ceiling 1162)` · `pm-dispatch/SKILL.md is 971 lines (ceiling 1005)` |
| `pnpm check:pm-governed-prose` | 0 | `✓ 2 instruction surface(s) name all 5 registered governed surfaces … and claim no others` |
| `pnpm check:skill-frame-sync` | 0 | `binding sentence present in all 2; 5 count mention(s) agree` |
| `pnpm check:pm-skill-id-lint` | 0 | `✓ check-skill-id-lint: 23 file(s) clean` |
| `pnpm check:pm-dispatch-gates` | 0 | `✓ dispatch-gates self-test: 1353 cases pass.` |
| `pnpm check:pm-governed-merges` | 0 | `✓ check-governed-merges --self-test: 245 assertions` |
| `pnpm check:doc-authoring` | 0 | `✓ 14730 customer-facing string(s) … clean` |
| `pnpm check:nul-bytes` | 0 | `check-nul-bytes: OK (… no raw ASCII control bytes)` |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint run check:doc-formula-expressions` | 0 | green after building the closure it needs (`@objectstack/lint...`); it exits 3 = PREREQUISITE NOT MET on an unbuilt tree |
| the other 20 derived families | 0 | all green |
| `pnpm lint` (whole repo, through the shared verify lock) | 0 | `os-verify-lock: VERDICT command-exit 0 · held the lock 73s` |

`node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --test` on the final five paths exits 3, which is the expected answer now:

```
governed-surface predicate: 4 of 5 path(s) hit the register (5 surfaces, repo-agnostic).
  ⛔  GOVERNED — a human merge is the review record for this PR (#9495 regime).
```

One reading worth surfacing, found while running these and **not** caused by this diff: `node scripts/check-required-contexts.mjs --verify-required-set`, once given `NODE_OPTIONS=--use-env-proxy` so the read reaches the API, reports `direction B — required in the live set, pinned by NO registry row (1): Governed Surface Queue Guard`. The check this PR changes is already a required context in the live ruleset with no `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` row pinning it. That is a pre-existing registry gap; it is reported to the PM rather than fixed here.
